open_points.subject: wall-clock versus elapsed-clock comparisons
open_points.text: “that one instant supplies ... every current-time comparison” and CLK-002 says the wall instant “decides every current-time comparison”; the elapsed clock nevertheless “measures the viewer-entry rate-limit window” and its boundary decision follows that reading
open_points.question: Is the A25 viewer-entry rate-limit comparison an exception to the rule that the wall-clock instant decides every current-time comparison?
options: Use the elapsed-clock reading for the rate-limit comparison as a stated exception
Use the wall-clock instant because every current-time comparison must use it
open_points.default_guess: Treat the elapsed-clock rule as the more specific rule and add an explicit exception for the rate-limit comparison.

witness.initial: A viewer-entry rate-limit window is open immediately before its boundary; the wall clock and monotonic clock do not place the request on the same side of that boundary.
events: A viewer submits an entry request.
The clock source returns one wall-clock instant and one elapsed-clock reading.
outcomes: The request is admitted or refused according to the elapsed reading.
The request is admitted or refused according to the wall-clock instant.
witness.observer: The viewer and the viewer-entry rate-limit test

open_points.subject: wall readings by clock-independent operations
open_points.text: CLK-002 says “an operation takes one wall reading,” while the Required tests cover “a test per time-dependent operation” and the normative introduction describes the reading as being “for its own timestamps”
open_points.question: Must an operation that writes no timestamp and makes no current-time comparison still take exactly one wall-clock reading, or must it take none?
options: Every portal operation takes exactly one wall reading
Only operations needing a timestamp or current-time comparison take one wall reading; clock-independent operations take none
open_points.default_guess: Read the requirement as applying only to time-dependent operations.

witness.initial: The service is running and its public liveness endpoint needs no timestamp or expiry decision.
events: A counting clock source records whether the operation requests wall time.
outcomes: The liveness operation reads the wall clock exactly once under CLK-002’s unqualified wording.
The liveness operation reads it zero times because it is not time-dependent and has no timestamp.
witness.observer: A counting-clock conformance test or runtime instrumentation

open_points.subject: CLK-002 witness binding
open_points.text: The witness line binds only CLK-001: “CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal]”
open_points.question: Which existing witness check is bound to the CLK-002 Required tests item and asserts CLK-002?
options: Bind CLK-002 to an existing named verification check
Add a distinct named verification check for CLK-002
open_points.default_guess: Add a dedicated CLK-002 verification check covering clock ownership and reading counts.

open_points.subject: CLK-002 host-clock source check
open_points.text: The Required test prohibits calls to a listed set of clock functions “and their variants,” but does not define which APIs, aliases, wrappers, native calls, or equivalent clocks count as variants
open_points.question: What exact calls and access patterns must the source check reject as host-clock variants?
options: Reject only the explicitly listed functions and aliases of those functions
Reject every wall- or elapsed-clock API, including equivalent APIs such as perf_counter and indirect wrappers outside the clock source
open_points.default_guess: Reject all direct or indirect host wall/elapsed-clock access outside the clock source, with an explicit closed list of recognized APIs and alias handling.

witness.initial: A module outside the clock source calls time.perf_counter() to make a duration-based decision.
events: The CLK-002 source check scans the module.
One implementation treats perf_counter as a time.monotonic variant; another limits the check to the functions explicitly named.
outcomes: The check fails because the module reads a host elapsed clock.
The check passes because perf_counter is not one of the enumerated function names.

open_points.subject: security-review dependency scope
open_points.text: The dependency category says “affected: deploy/requirements.txt (fastapi, pydantic, argon2-cffi, uvicorn pinned),” while changed A32 makes every distribution installed in the built image, including libraries pip resolves, part of the vulnerability decision
open_points.question: Does the State 2 security review’s dependency category cover every installed resolved distribution, or only the four direct pins named in deploy/requirements.txt?
options: Expand the affected scope to the complete installed distribution set judged by A32
Keep the security-review scope limited to the four direct pins
open_points.default_guess: Expand the security-review affected scope to the complete installed distribution set.

witness.initial: The four direct pins have no OSV vulnerability, but one transitive distribution installed by pip has a non-withdrawn OSV entry affecting its installed version.
events: The security-review dependency category is evaluated.
The A32 deployment gate evaluates the same image.
outcomes: A review scoped to the named requirements file reports the dependency category resolved while omitting the vulnerable transitive distribution.
A review scoped to A32’s installed set identifies the transitive distribution as affected and the deploy is blocked.
witness.observer: The security reviewer and deployment operator

open_points.subject: failed vulnerability-check recovery
open_points.text: “A check that cannot complete does not pass, and the deploy waits” appears together with “Each deploy makes one check”
open_points.question: After that one check cannot complete, can the same waiting deploy retry and eventually start, or can it proceed only through a new deploy with a new single check?
options: The same deploy may retry while waiting; define those attempts as part of its one check
The failed deploy can never start; recovery requires a new deploy and its new check
The deploy remains pending until an external completion of the original check supplies a verdict, without rerunning it
open_points.default_guess: Treat retries as attempts within one deployment-gate check and start only when that check obtains a complete passing verdict.

witness.initial: A built image is ready, but OSV is temporarily unreachable when its deploy performs the required check.
events: The check cannot complete, so deployment waits.
OSV becomes reachable without any image change or new deploy request.
outcomes: The same deploy retries or resumes its check, obtains a passing verdict, and starts the service.
The same deploy remains unable to start because its sole check already failed; an operator must initiate a new deploy.
